book: Zacharias Ursinus, Doctrinae christianae compendium (Heidelberg, 1584): one Latin work with a dedication, preface, Beza's verses and a page-numbered index up front, then a Prolegomena on Scripture and three parts of doctrine (human misery and liberation, gratitude), built as loci, subsections and catechism-style questions.
